title: Patchwalk cleanup review: obsolete hints, duplicate snapshots, and trial scaffolding
request: Review the current code for cleanup that is no longer relevant, and provide a review in Patchwalk before changing source.

overview.summary: Four scoped cleanup opportunities. First fix obsolete status-message checks that currently suppress useful navigation hints. Then reduce redundant representations in newly saved history, remove or explicitly configure the old workspace-specific toolchain fallback, and consider archiving unused miniLLM trial evidence. This is a plan, not implemented changes; the checkout remains clean.
overview.architecture: The viewer renders App state, while review.rs produces status and persists immutable review-round provenance. Presentation should not infer notification state from obsolete persistence strings. History should retain exact canonical inputs and preserve old rounds without repeatedly storing derived export formats. Source launch/install scripts should express supported toolchain requirements without assuming a particular scratch directory. Bundled demo/examples remain product assets; trial evidence is separate.
questions: Do any external tools consume the redundant derived round.context fields? None were found in this repository; keep existing historical context untouched.
Should the miniLLM trial outputs be retained as a documented integration example or archived outside the product repository?

annotations.title: Fix obsolete message checks that suppress navigation hints
annotations.intent: Replace the obsolete Read-only / Loaded saved review string checks in both overview and code panes with a shared way to distinguish normal review status from actionable notifications. Add focused rendering coverage for fresh and reopened reviews.
annotations.rationale: project_review now emits Review notes stay local and Loaded shared review. Both current UI checks classify these normal statuses as transient, so overview navigation/scroll hints and code location information are replaced indefinitely. A stale string comparison survives from the earlier persistence implementation.
alternatives: Update the two string literals directly for a smaller fix, but that leaves two rendering sites coupled to exact wording.

related.label: Same stale check in the code pane
Actual messages from the history layer

annotations.title: Stop generating redundant context-export representations
annotations.intent: For newly created review rounds, retain the original proposal_document, exact per-file source or before/after text, working-tree modes and provenance. Stop also serializing reconstructed proposal summaries, duplicate source line arrays and rendered diff-line records. Preserve existing round context values untouched.
annotations.rationale: No production consumer reads the derived context fields; rounds retain context as opaque JSON. The snapshot currently duplicates proposal_document with a reconstructed proposal object, source text with source arrays, and before/after strings with diff lines. These representations resemble the removed context-export workflow and inflate every saved round. Exact raw text and proposal JSON remain necessary for provenance.
alternatives: Keep all representations for undocumented external readers; if that compatibility is desired, document it rather than treating context as private history.

annotations.intent: Remove the hard-coded sibling ../.toolchain discovery from the launcher and installer, or replace it with a documented explicit override if still useful. Use one consistent toolchain selection rule and update the README. Keep run.sh as a convenient source launcher.
annotations.rationale: The checkout now lives under ~/Developer/github/joejstuart/patchwalk, where the assumed sibling .toolchain directory does not exist. Cargo is also absent from this session PATH. This workspace-specific branch no longer serves the moved checkout and is duplicated in both scripts. The installed standalone binary works independently; removing this branch is cleanup, not a way to avoid the source-build Rust prerequisite.
alternatives: Retain the fallback for the old compatibility-link path, but document it as a local development convenience rather than general installation behavior.

if [ -x "$local_toolchain/cargo/bin/cargo" ]; then
    export CARGO_HOME="$local_toolchain/cargo"
    export RUSTUP_HOME="$local_toolchain/rustup"

command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'Rust is required to build. Install it from https://rustup.rs and retry.' >&2; exit 1; }

To uninstall, remove the installed binary and `patchwalk` skill directory.
The launcher `./run.sh` also works without installation. Both scripts use this
workspace's isolated Rust toolchain when available, otherwise Cargo on PATH.
For a fresh machine, install Rust from [rustup.rs](https://rustup.rs) first.
The first build takes longer. macOS and Linux are the supported shell-install
paths; no prebuilt release downloads are published by this checkout.

With Cargo on PATH, `cargo install --path . --locked` is another way to install
the binary, usually into `~/.cargo/bin`; install the skill separately if wanted.
A built binary can also be copied to another machine of the same OS and CPU
architecture. The demo, schemas, and generation guides travel with it.

annotations.title: Archive miniLLM experiment outputs outside the shipped tool
annotations.intent: Review the proposals/minillm trial outputs for archival outside the product repository, then remove their two experiment-specific ignore entries if those directories are no longer maintained. Retain the generic demo and examples.
annotations.rationale: Searches of source, tests, prompts, skill and documentation found no consumers of the miniLLM proposal/snapshot/verification artifacts. Their directory-specific ignore rules are remnants of an earlier trial. This is optional repository hygiene; it is not unused runtime code, and experiment evidence should be archived rather than silently discarded.
alternatives: Keep one documented, portable example if the trial is useful as an integration case; remove or relocate machine-specific evidence files.

related.label: Generic demo remains a maintained example
